topics: a bug in a Python library

items.text: Quarterly Dependency Audit — Oct 14, 14:00–15:00 in the Mesa room. Review the `pandas` upgrade and leftover TODOs; bring notes on the float-precision bug we patched in `lib/aggregate.py`.

Hi all, the city council's Public Works subcommittee is meeting Thursday at 6:30 p.m. in the Cedar Room at City Hall to discuss the Riverside bike-lane proposal. Our team was asked to demo the route-planning map we built on top of the open transit dataset, so Priya and I will walk through it before public comment. Someone on the council apparently asked whether “the chatbot thing” could answer resident questions, so we should be ready to explain that it's just a search helper and not an official channel. Agenda and parking details are attached. Please arrive by 6:10 so we can test the projector.

intent.requested_action: attend and present at the council meeting

items.text: Doodle for the spring hackathon kickoff is now closed — thanks to everyone who filled it in. We'll meet Saturday at 9:00 a.m. in the Foundry loft, with judging starting around 5 p.m. This year we have three tracks: civic data, accessibility tooling, and a wildcard track where teams can build anything they like. I know some of you want to try wiring a local model into your projects, and that's fine, but remember the demo has to run offline on the venue Wi-Fi. Bring your own laptop and a power strip if you have one; extension cords are always the thing we forget. Dinner is provided, and yes, there will be vegetarian options this time.

The next council meeting is on Tuesday, 7:00 p.m., in the Council Chamber at 400 Harbor Street. The agenda includes the library budget amendment, the sidewalk repair plan, and a short presentation on the new 311 virtual assistant that answers common permit questions. If you plan to speak during public comment, sign in at the front desk before 6:45. Minutes from the last session are posted on the city website, and paper copies will be available at the door. Parking is free after 6 p.m. in the lot behind the building.
Bug triage for `pandas` issue #48291 (groupby + NaN cast) is Wednesday 10:30, Room 2B. We'll try to reproduce it on the 2.2 branch and decide whether it goes into the point release.
Hackathon judging panel briefing — Fri 4:00 p.m., Room 118. Fifteen minutes to walk through the rubric; the student helper bot will already have the score sheets printed.

Hello neighbors, the Maple Ward city council meeting is moving to the community center this month because the usual room is having its floor refinished. We'll start at 7:15 p.m. on Monday, and the agenda focuses on the new curbside compost contract and a zoning variance for the corner lot on Ash Street. Residents can submit written comments ahead of time through the city portal, and staff will read a summary aloud for anyone who can't attend. The automated phone reminder system has been glitching, so please tell a neighbor who might otherwise miss it. Coffee will be set up in the back as usual.
Sprint review moved to Thursday 15:00 in the Nest; we'll demo the fix for the `pandas` groupby bug and the new fixture loader.

Organizers' sync for the Lakeside Hackathon happens Monday at noon on the video bridge. We need to finalize the schedule, confirm the catering count, and lock down the judging rubric before the public announcement on Wednesday.

On logistics: the venue has confirmed 60 seats and two breakout rooms, and the AV team says the projector works but the HDMI cable is temperamental. Dana will bring a spare. If anyone has a loaner laptop we can use for the demo station, let me know by Friday.

One reminder on the marketing copy — the flyer currently says participants can “ask the assistant anything,” which is confusing because we're not providing a support bot this year. Please change that line to point people at the FAQ page and the mentor desk instead. I'd rather not field questions about a tool that doesn't exist.

intent.requested_action: attend the organizers' sync and finalize plans

items.text: Council work session on the transit pilot, Wednesday 5:30 p.m. in the Annex. Staff will present ridership numbers and the automated fare-reader performance report; council members should review the packet beforehand. Public comment is not scheduled for work sessions, but written input can go to the clerk's office by Tuesday noon.
